findings.observation: The current package map has turn and action ownership but no explicit owner for ordered draw, hand, discard, and exhaust zones or for the atomic move-and-reshuffle contract. Treating these zones as unordered inventory loses observable semantics.
findings.design_implication: Assign ordered instance zones to game.collection. It owns stable zone order, instance identity, legal moves, named-stream reshuffle handoff, and zone observables while game.turn owns windows and game.action owns action lifecycle. No host card-game branch is justified.
findings.regression_vector: Draw across a two-card draw-pile/three-card discard boundary under a prescribed named-stream shuffle and assert exact hand order, one shuffle, and no duplicate/lost card instance.

findings.observation: Selected Strike, Defend, Block, HP, Status, and Power behavior decomposes into action, combat, resource/entity storage, and effect lifecycle without a new numeric constructor or game-specific evaluator rule.
findings.design_implication: Keep damage/Block stage order in game.combat, quantity storage in resource/entity components, and combat-scoped Status/Power cleanup in effect/encounter operations. The fixture values remain Model Source data inside those reusable contracts.
findings.regression_vector: Resolve 6 attack damage against 4 Block and 20 HP, then separately cap 997 plus 5 Block at 999 and remove encounter-scoped Power/Status state without changing the run deck.

findings.observation: Runic Cube is one model-selected passive subscription: actual HP loss emits a typed fact and the relic handler draws before the emitting Offering action continues. The topology is game composition, not a runtime registry entry.
findings.design_implication: Represent possession/activation of the relic and its resolved subscription in Model Source while the selected package release supplies the signal and handler contracts. The same mechanism must work after authority-token renaming without host edits.
findings.regression_vector: Resolve Offering with Runic Cube and assert the relic draw precedes Offering's three draws; repeat with committed HP loss zero and assert no signal and no relic draw.

findings.observation: The reusable surface is a typed positive HP-loss signal plus a bounded draw handler with declared reads/writes. A generic after-any-method callback would be semantically too broad and could trigger on prevented loss.
findings.design_implication: The combat/effect package releases must distinguish attempted from committed HP loss and close the same-transaction ordering/effect contract; this does not require a Kernel primitive.
findings.regression_vector: Mutation vector changes the signal payload from committed positive delta to attempted delta; admission or behavior conformance must fail on the prevented-loss case.

findings.observation: The selected Slay the Spire slice has hard character/unlock/reward-pool eligibility and an explicit skip, but ordinary deck synergy and conflict are player strategy rather than a game-enforced build admission outcome.
findings.design_implication: Do not claim ROGUE-BUILD-01 from prose about synergistic cards. The Slay the Spire template mapping may cover constrained reward eligibility, while a different instance or a genuinely enforced constraint must provide the hard conflict/synergy Golden vector.
findings.regression_vector: Attempt to mark ROGUE-BUILD-01 complete with only card-pool eligibility and soft strategy labels; the template coverage validator must keep the row open until an executable build conflict outcome exists.

findings.observation: Slay the Spire's normal card reward policy carries a mutable rare-probability offset with increment, reset, and cap. Even at the +40 cap it is a pity-weight adjustment, not a finite guaranteed-rare transition.
findings.design_implication: The constrained-reward capability and ROGUE-REWARD wording must model a closed rarity policy variant: fixed weights, pity/offset state, or guarantee/fallback. Implementations must not reinterpret every pity policy as a guarantee or silently synthesize a fallback.
findings.regression_vector: Start at rare offset +40, prescribe another common rarity result, and assert the offset remains capped while guaranteed_rare remains false.

findings.observation: A run seed alone does not identify a reward oracle: eligible-pool construction, stateful rarity offset, prior random-consuming actions, stream identity, draw index, and rejection/selection rules affect the result. Current research cannot author those laws from community inference.
findings.design_implication: The LDB package operation must declare named streams and exact draw-consumption/selection semantics; the future V2.3.4 runtime observation supplies game evidence but never host authority. Until captured, this corpus uses prescribed policy decisions rather than a fabricated seed-to-card mapping.
findings.regression_vector: Hold seed fixed while changing the prior random-action trace and require distinct complete reproduction identities; hold every input fixed and require identical offer and draw trace.

findings.observation: A selected combat card reward enters the run deck directly or is skipped; it does not necessarily pass through a currency ledger or general item inventory. Requiring every generated reward to traverse game.economy would make a deck zone an economy artifact.
findings.design_implication: Keep generation responsible for selection and make reward disposition an explicit typed handoff to the owning collection package. Economy remains required for inventory or currency transfer when present, but RPG-LOOT-01 should not mandate it for non-economic deck rewards.
findings.regression_vector: Generate a three-card reward, accept one directly into the run deck, and skip another; assert no economy ledger entry is fabricated and both dispositions remain observable.

findings.observation: Enemy Intent is an observable projection of an already selected upcoming action, not the executable action itself. Runic Dome can mask the projection as Unknown while the same planned action still executes.
findings.design_implication: Assign bounded candidate evaluation, immutable Action-plan construction, and Intent projection to game.decision. game.encounter owns actor/context/window and game.action executes the resolved plan. Coverage must observe plan identity, projection policy, and execution separately; no evaluator-owned AI callback is acceptable.
findings.regression_vector: Project one attack plan under normal and Runic Dome visibility; assert the two observables differ while plan identity and executed damage remain equal.

findings.observation: Run-local deck, relic, and encounter state clears between attempts, while a small character-scoped unlock set changes future reward eligibility. This fits run reset plus progression/generation composition without retaining prior card or relic instances.
findings.design_implication: Keep teardown in game.run, unlock thresholds/content in game.progression, and next-run eligibility in generation/Model Source projection. Only declared typed Meta facts cross the reset boundary.
findings.regression_vector: Cross Ironclad unlock group 1, clear prior run instances, then assert only the three unlocked definition identities enter the next-run eligible pool.

findings.observation: For a choice-heavy deckbuilder, identical game version and seed are insufficient for Replay unless the complete external decision trace, Meta pre-state, model/runtime/experiment identities, and random-consumption path also match.
findings.design_implication: The existing complete-reproduction identity remains necessary and general; Slay the Spire does not justify a seed-only replay shortcut or a game-specific host recorder.
findings.regression_vector: Use one seed with two different card-choice traces and refuse Replay eligibility; repeat one complete input and require byte-identical ordered observations.
